newsitem.title: USA: NY/NJ Port Authority sets hearing on $1.2 bln bond.
newsitem.headline: NY/NJ Port Authority sets hearing on $1.2 bln bond.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey on Friday said it plans to hold hearings in mid-October on a plan to sell $1.2 billion of bonds to pay for a new international arrivals building at a New York airport.

The board of the bi-state agency, which has been criticized harshly by Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, who has argued that it favors New Jersey, might take up the bond proposal at its meeting on October 17, one day after the hearing.

A spokesman for the Authority declined to predict whether the board would approve the plan, but added that if it authorized the issue, by late November a bond prospectus likely would be ready, allowing an issue to be sold some time later.
The precise timing of any sale was not immediately available.
The spokesman, Bill Cahill, refuted speculation that the Authority's plans had been affected by the controversy with New York City's mayor, who has proposed splitting up the agency as a remedy.
A spokeswoman for Giuliani was not immediately available to comment.

"The timing isn't really coincidental with anything," said Bill Cahill, noting that in April two private developers were selected for the project, which the Board of Commissioners authorized in October 1994.
While the existing building opened in December 1957, it is out-moded because it was designed for smaller, propeller planes.
And it lacks the ability to shift airlines between different counters as they need them, which means passengers can end up with long walks to their gates that could have been avoided.
The new building will have a large number of retail stores, Cahill said.
